_note: Hand-authored. The film records which sheet the battery was working from; this file says what that sheet was and where a copy can be seen today. tools/build-map-sheets.mjs joins the two and fails on a sheet the film names that is not listed here, so the catalogue cannot quietly fall behind the transcription.
_basis: Only GSGS 4040 is named outright on a card — the correction of 20 January 1945. Every other series here is inferred from the scale and the country, and says so. An inferred series is a good guess, not a citation.

series.note: 134 sheets, designated by a letter and a number — R 3 is Marburg, S 1 is Bonn. This is the series the battery used for most of the war.

series.title: France 1:50,000
series.producer: Geographical Section, General Staff, War Office; Ordnance Survey
series.note: The Normandy and Northern France series, and the one the battery used from the beachhead to the Belgian border. Its sheets are designated by a grid square and a number — 6F/2 is St Lô, 10F/5 is Paris (West) — which is how the sheets named on the cards from July to September 1944 are identified as belonging to it.

_designations: The France sheets carry no series number on the cards, only a designation like 6F/2. They are assigned to GSGS 4250 because that series numbers its sheets exactly that way, and because one of them can be checked outright: the catalogued GSGS 4250 sheet 10F/5 is Paris (West), which is what the cards of 26 August to 12 September 1944 call it.

pariswest-10f5.note: The sheet the battery was on for the pursuit across the Seine, from the week Paris fell.

stlo-6e2.designationNote: St Lô is sheet 6F/2 in the GSGS 4250 index; there is no 6E/2 St Lô. Almost certainly the same sheet as stlo-6f2, misread once. Kept separate until the frame is read again.

stlo-6f2.note: The cards name two different sheets St Lô, 6E/2 and 6F/2, a fortnight apart. Only one of them can carry that name; which is not settled here.

domfront-2g1.designationNote: The card reads 2G, but the GSGS 4250 index puts this town on 7G — 2G is in Brittany, around Brest, which the battery was nowhere near. A 7 misread as a 2 on the film is the likely explanation. Left as transcribed, flagged here, and to be settled by re-reading the frame.

chimay-103.note: Numbered in the same sheet line as Vielsalm 93, the one sheet the film assigns to a series outright.

liege-9.note: The card gives no scale, and sheet 9 does not sit clearly in any of the Belgian sheet lines the battery used elsewhere. Placed in the 1:100,000 series as the least bad fit.

vielsalm-93n.note: The battery reported on this sheet for four days in January 1945 and then corrected itself: the position was on the 1:50,000 Vielsalm 93, not the 1:25,000 93 N.

aywaille-80se.note: Cards give this sheet at both 1:25,000 and 1:100,000. The Belgian sheet 80 SE is a 1:25,000 sheet, so the 1:100,000 readings are most likely the clerk carrying the wrong scale forward.

_repositories: Where these sheets can be seen. Checked 6 August 2026 from this machine; the status field records what answered and what did not, so the next person does not repeat the dead ends. A repository listed here is not a claim that it holds a particular sheet — per-sheet links live on the sheet itself, in sheets[].sources.

repositories.name: Battlefield Historian
repositories.holdings: Per-sheet catalogue pages for the GSGS series, with a scan preview. Its GSGS 4416 holding is 10 sheets of 134, and its GSGS 4250 holding does not include the Normandy sheets named on these cards.

repositories.name: WIG Map Archive (mapywig.org)
repositories.holdings: An open directory of Allied wartime series at full scanning resolution, including 762 sheets of GSGS 4416 / AMS M641 at 600 dpi. Many are McMaster University Library scans, mirrored here — which is how the sheets this project wanted were found while McMaster itself was down.

repositories.name: MAPSTER — Archiwum Map Wojskowego Instytutu Geograficznego
repositories.holdings: Scans of GSGS 4416 / AMS M641 at 300 dpi, largely digitised from the University of Texas collection. Its sheet index independently confirms the designations used here — R2 Siegen, R3 Marburg, S2 Koblenz.

repositories.name: Herder-Institut, Marburg — map catalogue
repositories.holdings: Catalogue of Central Europe 1:100,000, GSGS 4416 / AMS M641, M651 and M671, 1943-1949. Coverage runs heavily to the eastern sheets.

repositories.name: University of Texas Libraries — Perry-Castañeda Map Collection
repositories.holdings: The AMS sets, including Central Europe 1:100,000 (M641 / GSGS 4416). The originating collection for the MAPSTER scans of this series, whose file records name it outright.
